header.title: Warranty
header.desc: Warranty terms for dental treatment performed at Matikyan Dental Clinic.

warranty.policyTitle: The guarantee policy of Matikyan Dental Clinic
warranty.imageAlt: Dentist and patient reviewing warranty and treatment information at Matikyan Dental Clinic

items: Any warranty-related procedures are performed only in our clinic.
When warranty-related procedures are performed, the clinic does not cover accommodation in the country or transportation expenses.
Warranty for implantation is provided after prosthetic restoration.

sections.title: Warranty periods for different works
items: Restoration or rebuilding of a tooth with composite materials: 1 year.
Crowns and bridge prostheses: 3 years, except metal-plastic constructions.
Veneers and inlays: 2 years.
Full removable dentures: 2 years.
Clasp dentures: 3 years.
Implants after prosthetic restoration: 5 years.

sections.title: Full or partial suspension of warranty obligations
items: Insufficient or complete absence of oral hygiene.
The patient did not attend preventive check-ups twice a year.
Rules for using partial or removable dentures were not followed, including independent adjustment of the prosthesis.
Sudden changes in the patient's weight.
Trauma in the maxillofacial area.
Systemic diseases acquired during the warranty period, including diabetes, osteoporosis, or chemotherapy.
Violation of financial obligations to the clinic.

warranty.note: Patients wearing metal-ceramic constructions should be careful when eating hard and dry food such as crackers and walnuts, should not bite electrical wires, and should avoid consuming hot immediately after cold or cold immediately after hot.

header.title: Frequently Asked Questions
header.desc: Everything you want to know about our services, treatments, and what to expect at Matikyan Dental Clinic.

general.q: How often should I visit the dentist?
general.a: We recommend a routine check-up and professional cleaning every 6 months. Patients with gum disease, frequent cavities, or orthodontic appliances may need visits more often.

general.q: What should I bring to my first appointment?
general.a: Please bring a photo ID, insurance information if applicable, recent dental X-rays if available, and a list of current medications.
We try to accommodate dental emergencies the same day. For planned treatment, booking ahead is the best way to secure your preferred time.

treatments.a: Yes. Professional whitening is safe when it is carried out after an appropriate dental assessment and with materials suited to your teeth and gums.

treatments.q: How long do dental implants last?
treatments.a: With proper care, implants can serve for many years. Long-term success depends on oral hygiene, bone support, bite control, and regular follow-up visits.
Traditional porcelain veneers usually require some enamel preparation, so they are generally considered irreversible. We explain all conservative and restorative options during consultation.

treatments.q: How painful is a root canal?
treatments.a: Modern root canal treatment is typically managed comfortably with effective anesthesia. Most patients describe it as far easier than they expected.

payment.a: Insurance and reimbursement conditions depend on your provider and treatment type. Our team can review the expected details with you before care begins.
For more complex treatment plans, available payment arrangements can be discussed with the clinic team in advance.

payment.q: What is the cost of a consultation?
payment.a: Consultation costs depend on what is included in the visit, such as imaging or specialist assessment. We explain this clearly before scheduling.

orthodontics.q: Am I a candidate for Invisalign?
orthodontics.a: Invisalign is often suitable for mild to moderate crowding, spacing, and selected bite issues. A clinical exam and digital assessment are the best way to confirm whether it fits your case.

orthodontics.q: How long does Invisalign treatment take?
orthodontics.a: Treatment time depends on complexity, but many cases fall between 6 and 24 months. Your plan is based on the exact movements required.

dentalCleaningCheckup.title: Professional Oral Hygiene
dentalCleaningCheckup.tagline: Ultrasonic scaling, AirFlow, and preventive care
dentalCleaningCheckup.desc: Professional oral hygiene helps remove plaque, tartar, and surface stains using ultrasonic cleaning and AirFlow, while supporting healthier gums and cleaner teeth.
dentalCleaningCheckup.intro: Professional hygiene is one of the core therapeutic services at the clinic. It combines deposit removal, polishing, and preventive assessment to reduce inflammation and maintain oral health.
dentalCleaningCheckup.h2Description: The visit is designed to remove hard and soft deposits, improve hygiene access, and reduce factors that contribute to gum irritation and unpleasant breath.
process: Assessment of plaque, tartar, staining, and gum condition.
Ultrasonic removal of calculus and professional cleaning of tooth surfaces.
AirFlow polishing and hygiene recommendations based on your needs.
candidates: Patients with tartar buildup, staining, or bleeding gums.
Adults and teens due for professional oral hygiene.
Anyone preparing for restorative, orthodontic, or whitening treatment.
treatmentOptions: Ultrasonic scaling for hard deposits.
AirFlow polishing for surface stains and biofilm.
Personal hygiene guidance based on plaque and gum findings.
technology: Ultrasonic instruments are used to remove calculus from tooth surfaces.
AirFlow polishing helps clean surface staining and hard-to-reach areas.
Clinical assessment helps decide whether gum follow-up or related treatment is needed.
faqs: How often should I book professional oral hygiene?::The interval depends on plaque control, gum condition, tartar buildup, and any planned treatment.
Is AirFlow the same as whitening?::No. AirFlow removes external staining and biofilm, while whitening changes tooth shade with a separate clinical method.
Can hygiene help before implants or whitening?::Yes. Clean tooth and gum surfaces help make restorative, implant, orthodontic, or whitening planning more predictable.

teethWhitening.title: Teeth Whitening
teethWhitening.desc: Clinical whitening helps brighten teeth after shade assessment, using dentist-guided tray-based or light-activated methods depending on the case.
teethWhitening.intro: Whitening is offered after checking enamel condition, gum health, and the type of discoloration. The goal is safer, more even brightening with an approach suited to the patient.
teethWhitening.h2Description: Whitening planning starts with an examination and shade review so the method matches the condition of the teeth and the expected result.
process: Clinical shade assessment and suitability evaluation.
Tray-based whitening or light-activated whitening depending on indication.
Post-treatment advice to help maintain a brighter result.
candidates: Patients with external discoloration or age-related darkening.
Adults seeking a non-invasive aesthetic improvement.
Cases where existing restorations do not limit color matching.
treatmentOptions: Tray-based whitening after clinical assessment.
Light-activated whitening when it is suitable for the case.
Shade review and maintenance guidance after treatment.
technology: Shade assessment supports realistic whitening planning.
Dentist-supervised systems are selected according to enamel and gum condition.
Protective protocols help reduce unnecessary irritation during whitening.
faqs: Is teeth whitening suitable for everyone?::Suitability depends on enamel condition, gum health, sensitivity, restorations, and the type of discoloration.
Will fillings, crowns, or veneers whiten too?::No. Existing restorations do not change shade like natural enamel, so color matching may need planning.
How do I maintain the whitening result?::Maintenance depends on hygiene, diet, smoking habits, and follow-up advice from the dentist.

veneers.title: Dental Veneers & Aesthetic Restorations
veneers.tagline: Veneers, composite restorations, and tooth build-up
veneers.desc: Aesthetic dentistry improves visible tooth shape, color, and structure with veneers, composite restorations, and build-up when a tooth needs support before a crown.
veneers.intro: This service combines dental veneers with aesthetic restorations and tooth build-up. It is used when visible teeth need shape or color improvement, when damaged tooth structure must be restored, or when a tooth requires a stable base before prosthetic treatment.
veneers.h2Description: The treatment plan depends on enamel condition, remaining tooth structure, bite load, aesthetic goals, and whether a ceramic or composite solution is more appropriate.
process: Aesthetic consultation, shade review, and assessment of tooth structure.
Selection of ceramic veneers, composite veneers, tooth-colored restorations, or build-up.
Try-in, restoration, bonding, or preparation for the next prosthetic stage when needed.
candidates: Visible chips, spacing, discoloration, worn edges, or uneven contours.
Caries, fractures, old filling loss, or damaged tooth surfaces requiring aesthetic restoration.
Teeth that need build-up before a crown or broader prosthetic plan.
treatmentOptions: E.max, ceramic, and composite veneers for front-tooth aesthetics.
Composite bonding and tooth-colored restorations for selected defects.
Core build-up when a tooth needs support before a crown.
technology: Digital records or impressions support smile and restoration planning.
Adhesive restorative materials support conservative reconstruction when clinically possible.
Material selection considers bite, tooth structure, aesthetics, and future prosthetic needs.
faqs: When are veneers or aesthetic restorations recommended?::They are considered for visible discoloration, chips, spacing, worn edges, caries damage, or tooth structure loss.
Are ceramic veneers and composite restorations the same?::No. They differ in material, preparation, repair options, aesthetics, and long-term maintenance.
What is tooth build-up before a crown?::Build-up restores missing tooth structure so a future crown can have better support when the tooth is suitable for restoration.

dentalImplants.title: Dental Implants
dentalImplants.tagline: Implant placement with bone support options
dentalImplants.desc: Implant treatment restores missing teeth with surgical planning, implant placement, and supportive procedures such as bone grafting when indicated.
dentalImplants.intro: Implantology is part of the clinic’s surgical services. Treatment planning focuses on bone volume, implant position, soft tissues, and the future prosthetic restoration.
dentalImplants.h2Description: Successful implant treatment depends on diagnostics, surgical planning, healing conditions, and the quality of the final restoration.
process: Clinical evaluation and imaging to assess bone and implant feasibility.
Placement of a dental implant or mini-implant when indicated.
Restorative phase after healing, with additional support procedures if needed.
candidates: Patients missing one or more teeth.
Patients seeking a fixed alternative to removable prosthetics.
Cases that may also require bone augmentation before restoration.
treatmentOptions: Single-tooth implant placement after diagnostic planning.
Mini-implant options when clinically indicated.
Bone support procedures such as grafting when additional volume is required.
technology: Imaging helps evaluate bone volume, root anatomy, and implant position.
Surgical planning connects implant placement with the future crown or prosthesis.
Follow-up checks monitor healing before the restorative phase begins.
faqs: Who may need a dental implant?::Implants are considered for patients missing one or more teeth when bone, gum, and general conditions are suitable.
Why is diagnostics important before implants?::Diagnostics help evaluate bone volume, nearby anatomy, infection risk, and the future prosthetic plan.
Will I need a crown after the implant?::Usually the implant is restored with a crown, bridge, or prosthetic solution after the healing and planning stages.

prostheticsCrowns.title: Prosthetics & Crowns
prostheticsCrowns.tagline: Fixed, removable, and digitally planned restorations
prostheticsCrowns.desc: Orthopedic treatment includes crowns, removable prosthetics, and digitally planned restorative options for rebuilding chewing function and smile aesthetics.
prostheticsCrowns.intro: Orthopedic care covers both removable and fixed prosthetic solutions, from partial dentures to ceramic crowns and digitally planned restorations.
prostheticsCrowns.h2Description: The choice of restoration depends on the number of missing teeth, the condition of supporting teeth, bite requirements, and the desired material.
process: Removable prosthetics including rigid, soft, partial, non-acrylic, or clasp-based options.
Fixed restorations such as metal-ceramic, zirconia, zirconia-ceramic, and E.max crowns.
Digital orthopedics with 3Shape scanning and CAD/CAM-based planning.
candidates: Patients who need crowns, prosthetic rehabilitation, or material replacement.
Cases requiring removable or fixed restorative planning.
Patients who benefit from digital scanning and prosthetic design.
treatmentOptions: Metal-ceramic, zirconia, zirconia-ceramic, and E.max crown options.
Partial, clasp-based, non-acrylic, rigid, or soft removable prosthetics.
Digitally planned prosthetic restorations with scanning and CAD/CAM workflows.
technology: Digital scanning can improve records for prosthetic planning.
CAD/CAM modeling supports restoration design when used for the case.
Material selection considers bite, aesthetics, remaining teeth, and hygiene access.
faqs: When is a crown recommended?::A crown may be recommended when a tooth needs stronger coverage after damage, endodontic treatment, or structural loss.
How are crown materials selected?::Material choice depends on tooth location, bite load, aesthetics, opposing teeth, and clinical indications.
Are removable prosthetics still used?::Yes. Removable options may be appropriate when fixed treatment is not suitable or when several teeth require replacement.

rootCanalTreatment.title: Endodontic Treatment
rootCanalTreatment.desc: Endodontic treatment is used to manage pulpitis, infected canals, and internal tooth damage with cleaning, shaping, filling, and microscope-assisted precision when indicated.
rootCanalTreatment.intro: This service covers endodontic diagnosis and treatment of root canal systems when inflammation or infection has reached the inner tissues of the tooth.
rootCanalTreatment.h2Description: The aim is to disinfect and fill the canals thoroughly while preserving the tooth whenever a predictable restorative result is possible.
process: Diagnosis of pulpitis or canal infection with imaging and clinical testing.
Mechanical and chemical cleaning of the root canal system.
Filling and sealing of the canals, including treatment under a microscope when indicated.
candidates: Deep caries, pulpitis, or previously treated canals needing retreatment.
Pain, lingering sensitivity, or infection around the tooth root.
Teeth that need canal treatment before restoration or prosthetics.
treatmentOptions: Treatment of pulpitis and infected root canals.
Cleaning, shaping, and filling of root canal systems.
Microscope-assisted treatment or retreatment when indicated.
technology: Imaging helps evaluate canal anatomy and infection around the root.
Magnification can support more detailed canal access and cleaning in selected cases.
Canal sealing aims to preserve the tooth when restoration remains predictable.
faqs: When is root canal treatment needed?::It may be needed when inflammation or infection reaches the pulp or root canal system.
Can root canal treatment save every tooth?::No. Prognosis depends on tooth structure, infection, cracks, bone support, and restorative options.
Why might a crown be discussed after endodontics?::A tooth treated endodontically may need additional structural protection depending on remaining tooth tissue.

periodontalTreatment.title: Periodontal Treatment
periodontalTreatment.desc: Periodontal care focuses on diagnosing and treating gum inflammation and supporting structures, from non-surgical therapy to periodontal surgery when required.
periodontalTreatment.intro: This department treats gingivitis, periodontitis, and the consequences of periodontal inflammation using both conservative and surgical approaches based on the case.
periodontalTreatment.h2Description: Management depends on the stage of inflammation, pocket depth, tooth mobility, and the response of surrounding tissues to treatment.
process: Assessment of gum inflammation, periodontal pockets, and tooth stability.
Closed or open curettage, splinting, and supportive periodontal therapy.
Periodontal surgical procedures and adjunctive care such as plasma therapy when indicated.
candidates: Bleeding gums, swelling, bad breath, or gum recession.
Diagnosed gingivitis or periodontitis.
Teeth with mobility or supporting tissue loss that require specialist care.
treatmentOptions: Gingivitis and periodontitis assessment and management.
Closed or open curettage when clinically indicated.
Splinting, periodontal surgery, or adjunctive care based on tissue condition.
technology: Periodontal assessment evaluates pocket depth, bleeding, mobility, and tissue response.
Imaging may help assess bone support around teeth.
Maintenance planning helps reduce recurrence risk after active treatment.
faqs: What signs may indicate gum disease?::Bleeding, swelling, bad breath, gum recession, sensitivity, or tooth mobility can indicate periodontal problems.
Is professional hygiene enough for periodontitis?::Not always. Periodontitis may require deeper periodontal therapy, monitoring, and maintenance care.
Can periodontal health affect implants?::Yes. Gum and bone health are important before and after implant treatment.

oralSurgery.title: Oral Surgery
oralSurgery.tagline: Extractions, apicoectomy, sinus lift, and bone grafting
oralSurgery.desc: Oral surgical care includes tooth extractions, root-end surgery, sinus lift procedures, and bone grafting based on the patient’s clinical needs.
oralSurgery.intro: Surgical treatment is planned according to the tooth position, bone condition, infection status, and the future restorative goal, including implant preparation when needed.
oralSurgery.h2Description: The surgical plan depends on whether the case involves extraction, apical surgery, sinus augmentation, or reconstruction of bone volume before restoration.
process: Simple or complex tooth extraction based on tooth position and anatomy.
Apicoectomy for selected endodontic cases involving the root apex.
Sinus lift and bone grafting when additional bone support is needed.
candidates: Teeth that cannot be predictably preserved.
Surgical endodontic cases or chronic apical pathology.
Implant cases requiring sinus augmentation or bone reconstruction.
treatmentOptions: Simple or complex tooth extraction.
Apicoectomy for selected root-end problems.
Sinus lift or bone grafting when needed for future restoration or implants.
technology: Imaging helps evaluate tooth position, roots, bone, and nearby structures.
Surgical planning is adapted to infection status, anatomy, and future restoration needs.
Postoperative instructions support healing and reduce avoidable complications.
faqs: When is oral surgery recommended?::Surgery may be recommended for teeth that cannot be preserved, root-end pathology, bone reconstruction, or implant preparation.
Is every wisdom tooth removed?::No. Removal depends on position, symptoms, infection risk, and the effect on nearby teeth or tissues.
Why might bone grafting be needed?::Bone grafting may be considered when additional bone support is needed for healing or future implant planning.

orthodontics.title: Orthodontics
orthodontics.tagline: Clear aligners and braces for guided tooth movement
orthodontics.desc: Orthodontic treatment helps correct tooth alignment, spacing, crowding, and selected bite problems using clear aligners or fixed braces depending on the case.
orthodontics.intro: Orthodontics combines diagnosis, planning, and staged tooth movement to improve alignment and bite function. The treatment approach may involve removable clear aligners or fixed braces depending on the clinical situation.
orthodontics.h2Description: The choice between aligners and braces depends on crowding, spacing, bite correction needs, oral hygiene, and the level of movement control required.
process: Clinical assessment and digital records to define alignment and bite goals.
Selection of clear aligners or braces based on the complexity and required control.
Regular progress checks and refinements or adjustments during active treatment.
candidates: Adults and teens with crowding, spacing, or tooth-position concerns.
Patients comparing clear aligners with fixed braces.
Cases where bite correction and long-term stability need orthodontic planning.
treatmentOptions: Clear aligners for selected crowding, spacing, and low-visibility treatment needs.
Braces systems for fixed orthodontic control and more complex movement.
Regular monitoring, refinements, or adjustments during active treatment.
technology: Digital scanning supports orthodontic records and planning.
Staged planning helps define the sequence of tooth movement.
Progress visits help evaluate fit, wear compliance, bracket adjustments, and treatment response.
faqs: Are clear aligners or braces better?::The better option depends on bite, crowding, spacing, treatment complexity, and how much fixed control is needed.
Are aligners suitable for every case?::No. Some cases need braces or a different orthodontic plan for predictable movement.
Does orthodontic treatment require special hygiene?::Yes. Both aligners and braces require careful home care, and professional hygiene helps reduce plaque during treatment.

digitalDiagnostics.title: Diagnostics & Digital Dentistry
digitalDiagnostics.tagline: RVG, panoramic imaging, 3D CT, and digital treatment planning
digitalDiagnostics.desc: Digital diagnostics support precise dental treatment planning with targeted imaging and consultation, including RVG, panoramic imaging, and 3D CT when indicated.
digitalDiagnostics.intro: Diagnostics help define the condition of teeth, roots, bone, and surrounding structures before therapy, surgery, orthodontics, implants, or prosthetic work begins.
digitalDiagnostics.h2Description: The choice of imaging depends on the clinical question. The goal is to gather the information needed for a precise and safer treatment plan.
process: Clinical consultation and review of complaints, history, and treatment goals.
RVG imaging or panoramic radiography depending on the indication.
3D CT imaging for complex endodontic, surgical, implant, orthodontic, or prosthetic planning.
candidates: Patients starting new treatment or comparing treatment options.
Cases that need image-based evaluation before surgery, orthodontics, or implants.
Situations where detailed tooth, root, or bone assessment is important.
treatmentOptions: Clinical consultation and treatment planning.
RVG or panoramic imaging when indicated.
3D CT diagnostics for complex surgical, implant, endodontic, orthodontic, or prosthetic planning.
technology: RVG imaging provides targeted dental information with focused imaging.
Panoramic imaging helps review the broader dental and jaw situation.
3D CT can support more complex planning when two-dimensional imaging is not enough.
faqs: When is digital diagnostics needed?::It is used when clinical examination alone does not provide enough information for treatment planning.
Is every patient sent for 3D CT?::No. CT is used only when the clinical question requires three-dimensional information.
How does consultation help before treatment?::Consultation helps clarify diagnosis, compare treatment options, and plan the next step safely.
